units.sourceHTML: Values
units.originalInnerHTML: Values

units.sourceHTML: Values are the built-in atomic object types that all other objects are composed of. They can be created through literals, expressions that evaluate to a value. All values are immutable—once created, they do not change. The number ⟦CODE0⟧ is always the number ⟦CODE1⟧. The string ⟦CODE2⟧ can never have its character array modified in place.
units.originalInnerHTML: Values are the built-in atomic object types that all other objects are composed of. They can be created through literals, expressions that evaluate to a value. All values are immutable—once created, they do not change. The number 3 is always the number 3. The string "frozen" can never have its character array modified in place.

units.sourceHTML: A boolean value represents truth or falsehood. There are two boolean literals, ⟦CODE0⟧ and ⟦CODE1⟧. Their class is Bool.

units.sourceHTML: Raw strings #
units.originalInnerHTML: Raw strings #

units.sourceHTML:
A string literal can also be created using triple quotes ⟦CODE0⟧ which is
parsed as a raw string. A raw string is no different
from any other string, it’s just parsed in a different way.
units.originalInnerHTML: A string literal can also be created using triple quotes """ which is parsed as a raw string. A raw string is no different from any other string, it’s just parsed in a different way.

units.sourceHTML: Raw strings do not process escapes and do not apply any interpolation.
units.originalInnerHTML: Raw strings do not process escapes and do not apply any interpolation.

units.sourceHTML:
When a raw string spans multiple lines and a triple quote is on it’s own line,
any whitespace on that line will be ignored. This means the opening and closing
lines are not counted as part of the string when the triple quotes are separate lines,
as long as they only contain whitespace (spaces + tabs).

any whitespace on that line will be ignored. This means the opening and closing

units.sourceHTML:
A raw string will be parsed exactly as is in the file, unmodified.
This means it can contain quotes, invalid syntax, other data formats 
and so on without being modified by Wren.

units.sourceHTML: Ranges #
units.originalInnerHTML: Ranges #

units.originalInnerHTML: A range is a little object that represents a consecutive range of numbers. They don’t have their own dedicated literal syntax. Instead, the number class implements the .. and ... operators to create them:

units.sourceHTML:
This creates a range from three to eight, including eight itself. If you want a
half-inclusive range, use ⟦CODE0⟧:

You can pass them to a list’s subscript operator to return a subset of the list, for example, or on a String, the substring in that range:

units.sourceHTML: Null #
units.originalInnerHTML: Null #

units.sourceHTML: Wren has a special value ⟦CODE0⟧, which is the only instance of the class Null. (Note the difference in case.) It functions a bit like ⟦CODE1⟧ in some languages: it indicates the absence of a value. If you call a method that doesn’t return anything and get its returned value, you get ⟦CODE2⟧ back.
units.originalInnerHTML: Wren has a special value null, which is the only instance of the class Null. (Note the difference in case.) It functions a bit like void in some languages: it indicates the absence of a value. If you call a method that doesn’t return anything and get its returned value, you get null back.
